name: Tang Xizhong
current_role: Unverified; listed on Hurun China 2010 as head of Jingshi Group (zinc sulfate and lead)
profile: Tang Xizhong (唐锡中) appeared once on the Hurun China rich list in 2010, with wealth credited to Jingshi Group, a zinc sulfate and lead producer. I could not find any English or Chinese web coverage confirming the company's full name, location or his current role.
notes: I found almost nothing on him. English and Chinese searches for 唐锡中 and Jingshi Group plus zinc sulfate returned no matches. A Chinese company-registry lookup would be needed to identify the company. He has a single Hurun appearance (2010) and is likely low-profile.

name: Vishnukant Bhutada
current_role: Managing Director, Shilpa Medicare Ltd (Raichur, Karnataka)
profile: Vishnukant C. Bhutada is a first-generation pharma entrepreneur who founded Shilpa Medicare in his hometown of Raichur in 1987, at age 22, right after his B.Pharm. The company started with antibiotics, moved into oncology APIs and generics around 2000, and now sells globally. He remains Managing Director; Omprakash Inani is chairman.
interesting_fact: He came from a cotton-trading family but chose to build a pharma company in Raichur rather than a metro city: "I wanted to develop the region where I grew up." He started with Rs 50 lakh and 20 staff, and took the company public in 1994.
deep_cut_fact: His early export push targeted Bangladesh, which other Indian pharma firms ignored ("Nobody was focusing on Bangladesh back then"). Before a USFDA inspection of one API line, he added two more lines so inspectors would review all three at once.
notes: Low media profile. info@vbshilpa.com is the general company email. cs@vbshilpa.com is the company secretary's address (Ritu Tiwary), so the best route is a general corporate enquiry. His son Keshav Bhutada runs the subsidiary Shilpa Pharma Life Sciences.

name: N Srinivasan
current_role: Former VC & MD of India Cements (stepped down Dec 2024 after the UltraTech takeover). Promoter figure behind IPL team Chennai Super Kings.
profile: Narayanaswami Srinivasan (b. 1945, Tirunelveli) ran India Cements from 1989 and built it into a major South Indian cement producer. He was also a top cricket administrator: BCCI president and the ICC's first chairman. In December 2024 he sold the family's stake to UltraTech (Aditya Birla Group) and resigned as CEO & MD. He remains the figure most associated with Chennai Super Kings.
interesting_fact: After selling India Cements to UltraTech in 2024, he told staff the sale was driven by cost pressures, price wars and the inability to sell some land. The deal ended a family link to the company: his father, T.S. Narayanaswami, was one of India Cements' first employees.
deep_cut_fact: He has an MS in chemical engineering from the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago. He served two terms as Sheriff of Madras (1989–91), was president of the All India Chess Federation, and heads the Tamil Nadu Golf Federation.
notes: Well known in India because of cricket, and his cricket-administration years drew controversy, so outreach should stay on business and the industry. He has no personal website or social accounts that I could find. Best route is probably via Chennai Super Kings Cricket Ltd's corporate office. Source on his exit: https://www.dtnext.in/news/business/india-cements-promoter-n-srinivasan-steps-down-as-ultratech-completes-acquisition-816723

name: Chi Qinglin
current_role: Unknown; listed on Hurun China 2007–2008 with wealth from Orient Group (finance, building-materials retail, ports)
profile: Chi Qinglin (池清林) appeared on the Hurun China list in 2007–2008, with wealth credited to Orient Group, whose industries match the Harbin-based Orient Group (600811.SH). That group's founder and public face is Zhang Hongwei, and I found nothing that documents Chi Qinglin's role in it.
notes: I could not verify his identity. Searches for 池清林 returned only unrelated academics. If this is the Harbin Orient Group, note that the listed company entered court-supervised restructuring in 2024 (Caixin), so it is a sensitive topic. I found no contacts.

name: Xu Renliang
current_role: Unknown; listed on Hurun China 2005–2008 with wealth from New Zhongtian Holding Group (textiles)
profile: Xu Renliang (徐仁良) appeared on the Hurun China rich list from 2005 to 2008, with wealth credited to New Zhongtian Holding Group (新中天控股集团), a textile group. Web searches in English and Chinese did not surface the company's site, location or any current information on him.
notes: I could not verify his identity. The company should not be confused with Zhongtian Holding Group (中天控股集团, chaired by Lou Yongliang), which is a different company. A Chinese corporate-registry check would be needed. I found no contacts.

name: Prakash Amrut Mody
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Unichem Laboratories Ltd (now an Ipca Laboratories subsidiary)
profile: Dr. Prakash A. Mody (b. 1952) is the son of Unichem founder Amrut Mody and joined the board in 1974. He led the Mumbai drugmaker for decades and expanded it into 80+ countries. In 2017 he sold the domestic branded business to Torrent, and in 2023 he sold a 33.38% stake to Ipca Laboratories. He stepped down as MD in August 2023 and remains non-executive chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2017 Unichem sold its India branded-formulations business to Torrent Pharma and pivoted to exports and generics abroad. In 2023 Mody sold control to Ipca for about Rs 1,034 crore (announced price).
deep_cut_fact: He is a trained scientist with a Ph.D. in organic chemistry (after a Mumbai University post-graduate degree), an alumnus of Harvard Business School, and a former president of the Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance, the body of research-based Indian drugmakers.
notes: Low public profile. shares@unichemlabs.com is the company's shareholder or secretarial inbox, not a personal one. Since the Ipca deal, Unichem is controlled by Ipca, so his role is now non-executive.

name: Vijay Gupta
current_role: Likely Vijay Rajendraprasad Gupta, director (since 1993) of Surat Goods Transport Pvt Ltd, the parent of Mumbai-based Total Group logistics
profile: Surat Goods Transport (Total Group) is a Mumbai logistics group founded in 1963 by R. P. Gupta, covering road transport of normal, over-dimensional and project cargo, freight forwarding and bonded warehousing. The Hurun India 2019 entry for 'Vijay Gupta' most likely refers to Vijay Rajendraprasad Gupta, the longest-serving director on its board (since 1993).
interesting_fact: Total Group traces its origins to 1963, when R. P. Gupta founded Surat Goods Transport. It grew from road transport into freight forwarding, customs clearance and bonded warehouses in Mumbai and Delhi.
notes: The identity is likely but not confirmed: the name is very common, and the director match comes from the Tofler registry (https://www.tofler.in/surat-goods-transport-private-limited/company/U99999MH1977PTC020049). Vishal Gupta is described as Total Group's MD. The family is very private, so the best route is the general company email.

name: Earl H Nemser
current_role: Vice Chairman and Director, Interactive Brokers Group (IBKR)
profile: Earl H. Nemser is a securities and commodities lawyer (NYU economics; J.D. magna cum laude, Boston University) who has been a director or officer of Thomas Peterffy's IBKR companies since 1988 and Vice Chairman since 2006. He was a partner at Cadwalader and at Swidler Berlin, then special counsel at Dechert (2005–18), where he is now an independent advisor. His wealth comes from his long-held IBKR stake.
interesting_fact: He has been involved with Interactive Brokers' predecessor companies since 1988, nearly from the start of Peterffy's electronic-trading empire, and became Vice Chairman when the group prepared its 2007 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: He knew Thomas Peterffy before Interactive Brokers existed: in the 1970s he was outside counsel to Mocatta Metals, where Peterffy worked, and Institutional Investor quotes his recollections of that era. Institutional Investor calls him one of Peterffy's few close friends.
notes: Low-profile lawyer-director who rarely gives interviews. Best route is IBKR media relations (recent releases also list media@ibkr.com). His age is reported as late 70s.

name: Jeffrey N Simmons
current_role: President, CEO and Director, Elanco Animal Health (NYSE: ELAN)
profile: Jeff Simmons joined Elanco in 1989 straight out of Cornell and spent 30+ years in sales, marketing and R&D roles worldwide. He has led the company since 2008 and became CEO of the public company in 2018, when he steered its separation from Eli Lilly and NYSE listing. He then led the 2020 acquisition of Bayer Animal Health and the move to a new Indianapolis headquarters.
interesting_fact: He co-founded HATCH for Hunger, a donation-free model that supplies eggs to US food banks, and founded Edge Mentoring for leadership development. He also chaired the FFA Foundation board.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up on a wine-grape vineyard on Keuka Lake in New York's Finger Lakes; his father left the family dairy farm to start it. His dad's rule was that everyone had to leave for two years before coming back. He went to Cornell, chose Elanco for his 'two years', and never went back.
notes: Media-friendly CEO who does many interviews and podcasts (McKinsey, Semafor, ICE House, the University of Arkansas Be EPIC podcast) and talks often about food security and the human-animal bond. LinkedIn is the best direct route. His social accounts are linked from his official Elanco bio.

name: Chris Sugden
current_role: Managing Partner and Chair of the Investment Committee, Edison Partners (growth equity), based in Nashville
profile: Chris Sugden is a growth-equity investor who joined Edison Partners in 2002 and has been Managing Partner since 2011. He founded and leads its fintech team. He led Edison's investments in MoneyLion, including the 2018 $42M round, and sat on its board until Gen Digital acquired the company in April 2025. Before Edison he was CFO and division president of Princeton eCom.
interesting_fact: Over the last decade he has led exits of ten Edison portfolio companies with a combined enterprise value of over $15 billion. He has served as a director of 30+ companies.
deep_cut_fact: Away from venture capital, he serves on the Board of Commissioners of the Chattanooga Municipal Airport Authority and the board of the Michigan State University Research Foundation. He holds an honors accounting degree from Michigan State and credits his salesman father and grandfather with teaching him that "nothing happens without the first sale."
notes: His wealth listing comes from his MoneyLion insider holdings; Edison exited after the 2025 Gen Digital acquisition. His work email is published on his Edison bio, which makes him a very accessible VC and a good fit for fintech and entrepreneurship topics.

name: Jamie Foxx
current_role: Actor, musician, comedian and producer; founder of Foxxhole Productions (multiyear first-look deal with Fox Entertainment Studios)
profile: Jamie Foxx (born Eric Marlon Bishop, 1967, Terrell, Texas) is an Oscar-winning actor (Ray) and Grammy-winning musician who started in stand-up and In Living Color. He has hosted and executive-produced Fox's Beat Shazam since 2017. In 2026 he returned to music with the single 'Somebody' and is producing and starring in new films, including Amazon MGM's 'Deadlocked'.
interesting_fact: He picked the stage name 'Jamie Foxx' in 1989 for open-mic nights after noticing that female comics were often called up first, so he chose a gender-ambiguous first name. The surname is a tribute to Redd Foxx.
deep_cut_fact: Before Hollywood he was a classically trained pianist who started playing at age five, led the choir at New Hope Baptist Church in Terrell, and won a scholarship to study classical piano at United States International University. He was also the first quarterback at Terrell High to pass for more than 1,000 yards.
notes: An entertainer rather than a business founder; the angle for this podcast is his production company and his 2007 Sirius channel, The Foxxhole. Outreach normally goes through his agency or publicist, and I did not verify their current contacts. Avoid his 2023 hospitalization. jamiefoxx.com was unreachable when I checked.

name: Victor Nesi
current_role: Director, Stifel Financial Corp. (former Co-President and Head of the Institutional Group, 2014–2025)
profile: Victor J. Nesi is a veteran investment banker. He joined Stifel in 2009 and served as Co-President running the Institutional Group from 2014 until stepping back from operating duties on July 1, 2025, when he joined the board. He was previously Head of Americas Investment Banking at Merrill Lynch and global head of its TMT private equity group, and before that worked at Salomon Brothers and Goldman Sachs.
interesting_fact: Over a 35-year career he advised on strategic deals totalling more than $200 billion. He worked on the AT&T Wireless $10.6 billion tracking-stock carve-out, which was then the largest IPO in US history.
deep_cut_fact: Before banking, he practised corporate and securities law for four years at Shea & Gould, a once-prominent New York firm, after earning both his B.A. (1982) and J.D. (1985) at Georgetown.
notes: Now a non-executive director, so he may have more time for outside conversations. For press, Stifel's releases name Neil Shapiro as the media contact. He has a strong telecom and media banking background, which is relevant to data-center and infrastructure topics.

name: Daniel A Bergeron
current_role: Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, and Director, RBC Bearings Inc. (Oxford, Connecticut)
profile: Daniel A. Bergeron joined RBC Bearings in 2003 as VP Finance and became CFO the same year. He helped take the company public in 2005 and added the COO role in 2017. He gave up the CFO title in 2020 and now runs operations at the precision bearings and engineered components maker, which bought Dodge from ABB in 2021. He has been a director since 2013.
interesting_fact: He has spent more than two decades at RBC, first as CFO and then as COO, while the company grew into a large aerospace and industrial components supplier. His wealth comes mainly from long-held RBC stock.
deep_cut_fact: His career started in industrial finance: he spent 1987–1998 in financial reporting roles at Dorr-Oliver, a Connecticut maker of process equipment, and later was CFO of the telecom firm Paragon Networks International. He holds a finance B.S. from Northeastern and an MBA from the University of New Haven.
notes: A low-profile operating executive with very little media presence. I could not verify a current published IR or press email: the release pages returned 403. The best route is RBC's investor relations, via the contact block in its latest earnings release.

name: Joseph M Zubretsky
current_role: President and CEO, Molina Healthcare, Inc. (since November 2017; contract runs through at least 2027)
profile: Joe Zubretsky is a CPA-turned-insurance executive who has run Medicaid-focused insurer Molina Healthcare since 2017 and led its turnaround and growth. Before that he was CEO of The Hanover Group, and at Aetna he was CFO, head of national businesses and CEO of Healthagen. Earlier roles include Unum, Brera Capital and MassMutual. In 2026 he is steering Molina through Medicaid margin pressure and an exit from MAPD plans.
interesting_fact: Molina's 2025 proxy credits him with leading the company's turnaround and growth plans since he took over in 2017. In 2024 the board extended his contract to keep him through at least the end of 2027.
deep_cut_fact: He started as an accountant at Coopers & Lybrand, making partner in its national insurance practice, and remains a (inactive) CPA. He was CFO of MassMutual in 1997–99, then spent six years as a partner and CIO at the private equity firm Brera Capital before joining Unum and Aetna. He is a University of Hartford business graduate.
notes: Both emails are the media and IR contacts published in Molina's 2026 press releases, not his own. He is a frequent earnings-call speaker but does few podcasts. Molina's 2025–26 earnings misses are a sensitive topic.

name: Robert Symmes MacArthur
current_role: Managing Partner, Forager Capital Management, LLC (general partner of Forager Fund, L.P.)
profile: Robert MacArthur is a principal and managing partner of Forager Capital Management, a concentrated public-equity investment firm he runs with Edward Kissel. Through Forager Fund, L.P. he is a large holder of small caps such as Regional Management Corp. (about 10%) and MasterCraft Boat Holdings (6.0% as of mid-2026), which is why he appears as a ten-percent owner in SEC insider data.
interesting_fact: Forager runs a concentrated, activist-adjacent small-cap strategy. It reported a joint 6.0% stake (1.45M shares) in wakeboat maker MasterCraft and about 1.04M shares (roughly 10%) of consumer lender Regional Management.
notes: Very low public profile; I found no firm website, bio or social accounts. Forager Capital Management (US) is unrelated to Australia's Forager Funds. Its stake filings are at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1519401/000165495425006842/forager-rmcrobertmacarthu.htm. The only practical route is the business address in Forager's SEC filings.

name: Walter S Woltosz
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Simulations Plus, Inc. (chairman 1996–Dec 2024; company being acquired by Altaris for about $375M, expected to close Q4 2026)
profile: Walt Woltosz is an Auburn-trained aerospace engineer who spent 13 years building simulation and optimization software for rocket motors and missiles (Space Shuttle, AMRAAM, Pegasus). He then founded Words+ (1981), maker of PC-based communication systems for people who cannot speak, and Simulations Plus (1996), a Nasdaq-listed developer of ADME/PBPK modeling software for drug development. He was CEO until 2018 and is still a director.
interesting_fact: Stephen Hawking used Words+ software (Equalizer, later EZ Keys) to talk and write for decades. Woltosz said Hawking was the fastest user his team ever saw, reaching 20+ words per minute at his peak.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Words+ he worked with Northrop Services on simulation and optimization software for the Space Shuttle's ascent trajectory. Auburn credits his team with the first communication system to use adaptive word prediction (1986). He endowed Auburn Engineering's graduate fellowships, whose recipients are called 'Woltosz Fellows'.
notes: A strong guest for a founder story that runs from aerospace to assistive technology to pharma software. The Altaris take-private ($18.50/share) is pending, so company contact routes may change after closing. info@ is the general company inbox.
